newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM against front with rivals.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM against front with rivals.

text.p: Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on Friday rejected an offer to join an alliance headed by his main rival in the coalition government.
But the premier said his Cambodian People's Party (CPP) wanted to continue working with the royalist FUNCINPEC party of First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh in government and parliament.

"The CPP cannot join with any front because we are the CPP, a big party, and we cannot accept to join with any front, but we can cooperate with any party," he told reporters attending the opening day of the annual CPP congress.
"We continue with FUNCINPEC in government, in the national assembly, and we want to cooperate for the future," he added.

Ranariddh on Thursday confirmed plans to form a new political alliance, including Khmer Rouge defectors and the unrecognised opposition Khmer Nation Party, for elections due in 1998. He said the CPP could join if it wanted.

The prince denied the new Front Uni National (FUN -- United National Front) was aimed against the CPP, but analysts have said its formation would exacerbate tension in the uneasy coalition and could paralyse government.

FUNCINPEC and the formerly communist CPP formed an alliance after U.N.-run elections in 1993. Their uneasy relations have been strained recently by the royalists demand for a greater share of power and by their rival efforts to win the allegiance of thousands of Khmer Rouge defectors.

Hun Sen said representatives from eight former Khmer Rouge divisions and two brigades were attending the four-day CPP congress, which will map out strategy and appoint new members to its central committee.
"The reason that I decided to join the CPP is because the Cambodian people support this party," said Ieng Phat, a former Khmer Rouge commander in the northwest district of Samlaut.
